title: Coagulase Test
principle: Coagulase is an enzyme that converts fibrinogen in plasma to fibrin, causing visible clot formation. A slide test detects bound coagulase ('clumping factor') directly on the cell surface; a tube test detects free coagulase secreted into the surrounding plasma.
purpose: The classic test for presumptively distinguishing Staphylococcus aureus (typically coagulase-positive) from most other, coagulase-negative staphylococci.
reagents: Rabbit or human plasma with anticoagulant (e.g. EDTA plasma)

procedure.instruction: Slide test: emulsify a colony in a drop of water or saline on a slide, add a drop of plasma, and mix — observe within 10 seconds for clumping.
procedure.note: The slide test detects bound coagulase only; a negative slide test should be confirmed with a tube test before reporting coagulase-negative.

procedure.instruction: Tube test: emulsify a colony (or add broth culture) into a tube of plasma diluted per the manufacturer's instructions, and incubate at 35-37°C.
Examine the tube test at intervals (commonly checked at 1-4 hours) for clot formation, and again at 24 hours if still negative.
procedure.note: Some strains produce fibrinolysin, which can dissolve a clot that formed earlier — an early check that misses a transient clot can give a false negative if only read at 24 hours.

positiveResult: Slide test: visible clumping within 10 seconds. Tube test: any degree of visible clot formation (graded from a small clot to complete solid coagulation).
negativeResult: Slide test: no clumping. Tube test: fluid remains completely liquid at both the early check and 24 hours.
interpretation: A positive result (by either method, but the tube test is the definitive reference method) is strongly associated with Staphylococcus aureus; a negative result is consistent with most other Staphylococcus species but should be confirmed with the tube test if the slide test alone was negative.
precautions: Always confirm a negative slide test with a tube test before finalizing an identification.
Check tube tests at an early timepoint as well as 24 hours to catch clots later dissolved by fibrinolysin.
limitations: A small number of coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species and other genera can occasionally give unexpected results, so coagulase status is one identifying character among several, not a complete species identification on its own.
